intro_line: An ancient hilltop capital where Roman stones meet modern coffee shops.
intro: Amman rewards visitors with Roman ruins, a buzzing downtown and easy day trips across Jordan. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
transit_facts: No metro or tram; the BRT bus network is the fast backbone, about 0.610 JOD a ride.
City buses are cheap but often Arabic-only; pay exact fare or swipe a Visa or MasterCard.
Yellow and grey taxis use meters; most trips in town stay under 2-5 JOD.
Uber and Careem both work well in Amman; core rides cost about 1-4 JOD.
Driving is common but traffic is heavy; car rental desks are at the airport and in town.
Walking is patchy: steep hills, missing sidewalks and few crossings, so plan some rides. No ferry service.

airports.name: Queen Alia International Airport
airports.note: Main gateway for Jordan, about 26 km south of the centre.

options.note: Buy the ticket at the kiosk outside arrivals; cash is safest.
Take the bus to Tabarbour, then transfer to the BRT.
Fixed airport fare; pay by card at the taxi booth.
Pick up at the departures level upstairs.
